findings.reason: Proof step 4.1 uses the relaxed-objective definition to equate inf J with inf F over all finite nonnegative measures. That definition proves the equality only for lifts with finite integral of |w|. The feature-energy domain can also include finite-energy measures without that moment, for example when the constant penalty is zero and the feature map vanishes or decays. The theorem does not prove that truncations to bounded |w| approximate F. The smallest missing prerequisite is a truncation result showing F(μ restricted to |w|≤R) converges to F(μ) for every finite-energy lift. The affected consumers are this theorem's global-minimum conclusion and cor-partial-homogeneous-wasserstein-limit-is-global-minimizer.
